In this paper, we have described a parallel data collection effort involving 6k seed parallel sentences for 39 languages, and investigated the effects of this relatively small but high-quality dataset on machine translation performance.
datasets: GlobalVoices, Gnome, KDE, Sardware, Tatoeba, Ubuntu and Wikimedia corpora (OPUS)
models: Transformer (6 encoder / 6 decoder layers, 8 heads, 512 dim)
outputs: Translated sentences produced by the MT systems

quote: We report all results using automatic evaluation metrics against the FLORES-200 benchmark. We rely on the chrF++ score...
We rely on the chrF++ score , which is based on character-level n‑gram overlap, and is complemented by unigram and bigram features.

We report all results using automatic evaluation metrics against the FLORES-200 benchmark. We rely on the chrF++ score, which is based on character-level n-gram overlap, and is complemented by unigram and bigram features.
